name: desire for knowledge
quote: I'd like to know what's going on.
description: Wanting to better understand a particular aspect of the physical or social environment towards having better explanations and decisions.
perceptions: Having accurate and broad knowledge is important.
The more I understand, the better my explanations and decisions.
It may also improve my experience or standing with a social group.
results: You may seek ways to satisfy the curiosity

guidance.description: The internet lets you learn about anything. You should consider making sure that your teaching resource is reputable and up-to-date.

There is nothing actually stopping us from harnessing our curiosity. It’s really just about picking the right priorities and making a deliberate effort to learn, to have novel experiences, and to close the gap between what we know and want to know.

variations.name: desire to be correct
variations.description: Wanting to have your expectations or suspicions confirmed.
perceptions: In order to live in the world, I need to understand it.
My expectations and predictions are being tested all the time.
If I'm wrong about things, it must mean I don't understand that thing correctly.

variations.name: education
variations.description: Putting effort into learning something about the world that's not directly entertaining. This can be formal or informal, from media or a person, focused or sporadic.
perceptions: Understanding it will help me make better decisions or improve my standing with a social group.
Understanding it will take time and effort.

guidance.description: The internet lets you learn about anything. You should consider making sure that your teaching resource is reputable and up-to-date.

variations.name: story consumer
variations.description: Wanting to be exposed to a storyteller. We love tales, fables, books, movies, and games. We learn from them, we bond with others over them.
perceptions: I like stories because they're a fun social experience where you can learn about life and the social world.

guidance.description: A big part of engaging with fiction is to share the experience with others, so a good way to find stories is to ask your friends what they're reading or watching. Web or library searches for you favorite genres is another good way.

variations.name: curious about something
variations.description: A desire for a specific piece or category of knowledge.
perceptions: I would like to know the answer to a particular question.
Knowing this will help me make sense of something bigger.
examples: Wanting to know the ending of the story.
Wanting to know why rainbows are multi-colored.

comparisons.description: You can be curious about one thing (or category) without necessarily having a general thirst for knowledge.

commentaries.quote: A reader lives a thousand lives before he dies, said Jojen. The man who never reads lives only one.
No thief, however skillful, can rob one of knowledge, and that is why knowledge is the best and safest treasure to acquire.
I’ve learned one thing-people who know the least anyways seem to know it the loudest.

You are your greatest investment. The more you store in that mind of yours, the more you enrich your experience, the more people you meet, the more books you read, and the more places you visit, the greater is that investment in all that you are. Everything that you add to your peace of mind, and to your outlook upon life, is added capital that no one but yourself can dissipate.
Gossip isn't scandal and it's not merely malicious. It's chatter about the human race by lovers of the same.

Knowledge is the faceted lens that creates the light show of your innermost experience. Sensations and impulses bounce around your knowledge patterns to create either stunning mental laser shows or fuzzy twilight haze.
We so want to be right and so trust that our desire to be right is something that God would surely bless. Yet the desire to be right comes with a price: the fear of being wrong.
The cure for boredom is curiosity. There is no cure for curiosity.
Curiosity is like a metal detector. Over time, I have come to revere my curiosity for alerting me to my own personal gold.
